title: Looking back: year one
hookLine: the stories, the practices, the Dhammapada, the depths
tomorrow: every teacher says the others are wrong. who do you trust?

lines: AN OLD NOTEBOOK IN A DRAWER.
cards: An old notebook turns up at the back of a drawer: your own handwriting, younger, a bit unsure. The Buddha had a moment like that.
After a long stretch of pushing his body to the edge, starving himself until he could barely stand, the Majjhima Nikaya says, he stopped and remembered an afternoon from boyhood. His father was busy.
He was sitting in the cool shade of a rose-apple tree, and his mind went quiet, glad and settled, with no strain at all. And he asked himself: could that be the way?

teach.b: Yes, he saw. Then a second question: why am I afraid of that happiness? It has nothing to do with sensual pleasure.
So he ate again, got his strength back, and set out on what his first sermon would call the middle way, between pushing and indulging.
The path forward was hiding in a memory of the beginning. That's what the summit's first day does.

Year one of this path was the first mountain: the stories, the first small practices, the Dhammapada's opening verse, in Max Müller's words, "All that we are is the result of what we have thought," and a first taste of the depths.
Some of it may look simple from up here, the way a child's afternoon under a tree might have looked simple to a man who'd tried everything. The Buddha didn't climb past his beginning.
He went back to it and found the path inside it.

teach.h: SIX FESTIVALS, KEPT FOR THE ROAD.
teach.b: And the last week, kept for the road. Asalha: the wheel still turns. Obon: they come home.
Kathina: the rains end in gifts. Rohatsu: the morning star. Losar: a fresh year.
Magha Puja: the heart of it.
Five years in, the first mountain is still under your feet.

how: Buddhists retell the Buddha's life story at festivals and in temples, including the boyhood memory under the rose-apple tree that turned him toward the middle way.

he remembered a calm afternoon under a rose-apple tree and asked: could that be the way?
he asked himself why he feared a happiness that had nothing to do with sensual pleasure
then he ate again and sat down on the middle way.

games.q: after a long stretch of harsh practice that got him nowhere, what did the Buddha turn to next?
o: a calm afternoon he remembered from boyhood.
a harsher fast than any he'd tried before.
a new teacher with a brand-new method.
games.why: in MN 36 he remembers sitting in the shade of a rose-apple tree, glad and settled, and asks: could that be the way? it was.

practice: Close your eyes and let one moment from your first year on this path come back: a story that stuck, a line, a morning you sat. Don't grade it as small. Rest in it the way he rested in the shade, and notice what it still holds.

wordCard.voice: Looking back: the summit's first step, the way the Buddha found his path in one remembered afternoon.
